title: PaMCP baseline method and adapter registry
policy: Baseline names are not fidelity claims. `ready`, `partial_adapter`, `adapter_to_build` and `planned` distinguish implementation maturity.

comparison_tracks.retrieval: BM25, Dense-LSA, RAG-MCP, MCP-Zero, COLT-style, ToolScope-style, CMTF-style and per-subtask.
comparison_tracks.end_to_end: All methods run under the same task, prompt/model, visible registry, principal policy, token/time budget and evaluator; runtime methods also use the same sandbox/judge.
comparison_tracks.security: Progent/Fides/CaMeL are runtime security comparators, not retrieval baselines. Report both utility and enforcement outcome.
comparison_tracks.experience: AutoTool (AAAI 2026) is restricted to E21 and requires confirmed trajectory records.

fairness_protocol: Use identical query/task IDs, registry snapshot, server availability and visibility set.
Give baseline methods only information permitted by their method; evaluator gold labels are not available to discovery-time queries.
Fit all learned indexes, scene graphs and cluster thresholds on training/development data only; never train on test qrels.
Use same top-k/tool exposure budget where the method allows it; separately report stepwise frontier and cumulative union for planners.
Report native/official reproduction, clean-room implementation, adaptation and surrogate separately.
Preserve server::tool identity, provider, definition hash, effects and evidence through merger/adaptation layers.
For E13/E14 use the same real execution runtime, model, judge, tool budgets, timeout and injection cases.
Record exact commit, adapter version, parameter JSON, model/tokenizer version, seeds and raw rankings.

baselines.name: All-tools exposure
baselines.method: Expose the entire visible registry without filtering or ranking.

baselines.name: BM25 lexical retrieval
baselines.method: Rank tool names, server names, classes and descriptions with BM25; no model embedding, type closure or policy reasoning.

baselines.name: Dense retrieval (LSA surrogate)
baselines.method: Rank registry descriptions by cosine similarity using the repository's TF-IDF plus truncated-SVD encoder. This is a dense-retrieval surrogate, not BGE-M3.

baselines.name: RAG-MCP-style global top-k
baselines.method: Embed the whole request and return top-k tools from the global catalogue. No task decomposition, tool-set constraints or official upstream code reproduction is claimed.

baselines.name: MCP-Zero hierarchical routing
baselines.method: Route each goal to top server summaries, then rank tools within selected servers. Current adapter is single-pass; it does not reproduce MCP-Zero's LLM active-request loop or prompt protocol.

baselines.name: Per-subtask hybrid retrieval
baselines.method: Retrieve independently for each authored subgoal, then union candidate tools. Does not perform global toolkit composition or joint validation.

baselines.name: COLT-style completeness retrieval
baselines.method: Build query-tool and query-scene-tool co-use graphs from training queries only; rank tools with semantic relevance plus scene-neighbour support; optimize completeness-oriented top-k. Must use an explicit train split and never derive scenes from evaluation queries. Executable clean-room adapter is present in src/taas/experiments/baseline_runner.py; it is not a bit-for-bit reproduction.

baselines.name: ToolScope-style merger and contextual retrieval
baselines.method: Cluster candidate tools with a declared semantic-equivalence threshold, then context-rank within clusters. Preserve original provider/tool identities, hashes, effects and evidence; report merge precision, recall and false-equivalence rate. This clean-room adapter is not an exact reproduction of the paper's LLM merger/cross-encoder stack. Executable clean-room adapter is present in src/taas/experiments/baseline_runner.py; it is not a bit-for-bit reproduction.

baselines.name: CMTF state-frontier planning
baselines.method: Search typed precondition/effect states with breadth-first expansion; expose the next-step frontier and cumulative union. Adaptation maps TaaS semantic types/effects to planner states and must disclose how contracts were sourced. Executable clean-room adapter is present in src/taas/experiments/baseline_runner.py; it is not a bit-for-bit reproduction.

baselines.name: AutoTool (AAAI 2026) trajectory reuse
baselines.method: Retrieve and reuse confirmed historical execution trajectories, with registry/hash/policy revalidation before reuse. Only E21; do not confuse this with a differently named AutoTool publication. Executable clean-room adapter is present in src/taas/experiments/baseline_runner.py; it is not a bit-for-bit reproduction.

baselines.name: MCP default annotation reading
baselines.method: Expose the complete discovered tool catalogue as a default client would; surface published readOnlyHint/destructiveHint/openWorldHint values for the client/agent but do not treat them as an access-control decision or verified evidence.

baselines.name: Closed-world annotation filter
baselines.method: Closed-world read-only filter: require readOnlyHint=true; missing, false or malformed hints are ineligible. This is stricter than merely displaying MCP annotations.

baselines.name: Positive lexical evidence filter
baselines.method: Positive lexical filter: require an explicit read/list/get/search/fetch/retrieve-style cue and no lexically detected persistent state modification; lexical evidence is weak, not observed evidence.

baselines.name: Closed-world lexical filter
baselines.method: Closed-world lexical filter: reject explicit lexical write/delete/execute/money cues and treat the absence of such cues as safe. This intentionally exposes the risk of unknown-as-safe inference.

baselines.name: Observed/attested evidence eligibility
baselines.method: Use property-specific trust thresholds over hash-bound observed or attested evidence. The preview adapter remains blocked until independent evidence records and a verified evidence-store snapshot are supplied; it must not substitute annotations, lexical inference or evaluation labels.

baselines.name: Progent-style runtime policy enforcement
baselines.method: Enforce per-tool effect and argument restrictions immediately before invocation; report denial/fallback and policy-update behavior separately from retrieval quality.

baselines.name: Fides-style information-flow control
baselines.method: Propagate confidentiality/integrity labels through tool inputs and outputs and enforce declassification/output policies. Not a retrieval baseline.

baselines.name: CaMeL-style taint and capability enforcement
baselines.method: Track data dependency labels and check tool-call policies at the interpreter boundary. Requires an agent interpreter/runtime integration; not a retrieval baseline.

baselines.name: Linear eligibility scan
baselines.method: Scan every tool/property record to compute eligibility; compare with bitmap eligibility under identical policy semantics.

baselines.name: Full registry rebuild
baselines.method: Rebuild all contracts, hypergraph, retrieval structures and eligibility state from a complete post-event registry snapshot. A dedicated E16 event-replay worker is still required; the preview API does not simulate registry notifications.

baselines.name: No counterexample-guided refinement
baselines.method: Run Full PaMCP with counterexample-guided refinement disabled (refine_k=0); preserve G, P and S. Used as an isolated E17/E18 component control.

baselines.name: Unverified model self-assessment
baselines.method: Use model-declared capability/confidence without external calibration; report it only as a self-assessment control.

baselines.name: Strict uncalibrated model profile
baselines.method: Run with a strict uncalibrated profile assigning zero native capability to unmeasured classes. A dedicated profile-comparison adapter is still required for the E11/E12/E19 study.

baselines.name: Empirically calibrated model profile
baselines.method: Use a frozen, empirically calibrated model profile with a dataset/version hash and calibration report. The profile-comparison adapter and calibration-artifact validation remain to be implemented.

baselines.name: No trajectory experience reuse
baselines.method: Use per-subtask retrieval without consulting a trajectory repository. This is the zero-experience control for the E21 trajectory-reuse comparison.

baselines.name: Structural schema typing
baselines.method: Infer semantic input/output types from JSON Schema primitive types, required fields and schema structure only.

baselines.name: Schema plus lexical typing
baselines.method: Combine schema-derived types with names, argument names and descriptions; no human labels or runtime probe evidence.

baselines.name: LLM-assisted semantic typing
baselines.method: Generate typed input/output contracts from public schemas and descriptions, then compare against blinded human annotations; evaluator labels are not prompt inputs.

baselines.name: Published effect declarations
baselines.method: Infer effect claims only from MCP annotations; missing annotations remain unknown, and declaration truth is assessed against independent probe/human labels.

baselines.name: Lexical effect inference
baselines.method: Infer candidate effect classes from tool names, descriptions and argument names using fixed transparent lexical rules.

baselines.name: Observed effect probing
baselines.method: Execute bounded, credential-free test calls in isolated reference servers; infer observed effects from before/after state and traces. Never derive observed evidence from evaluation labels.
